intro.title: What is Pub Street?
intro.description: Pub Street is the most famous nightlife area in Siem Reap, Cambodia. Tucked beside the Old Market (Phsar Chas) in the city center, it is where visitors gather after dark to eat, drink and enjoy the easygoing atmosphere of a Cambodian travel town.

facts.v: Old Market area, central Siem Reap

items.text: The best-known nightlife hub in Siem Reap.
Steps from the Old Market and the Siem Reap River.
Restaurants, bars, street food and shops in one place.

guide.description: A quick orientation before you go.

items.text: Free to walk around — no entry ticket.
Easily reached on foot from the city center.
Liveliest from around 18:00 to midnight.
Family-friendly earlier in the evening.

history.title: History & Culture
history.subtitle: How a quiet riverside town grew into Cambodia's best-known travel nightlife district.

sections.title: A quiet riverside town
sections.text: Siem Reap was a small provincial town. The temples of Angkor were already famous, but visitor infrastructure was limited and nightlife was minimal.

sections.title: Pub Street takes shape
sections.text: As international arrivals grew, the strip near the Old Market transformed into restaurants and bars. The area became a pedestrian-friendly evening zone for visitors.

sections.title: Siem Reap's social heart
sections.text: Pub Street is now the city's gathering point after dark — live music, street performances and a blend of Khmer and traveler culture.

history.legendText: Locals say there is an unwritten rule: after a day at the temples, every traveller returns to the old town at dusk to wash off the dust among lights and aromas. Over time, this short street between the Old Market and the river became the ritual “return to the human world” after pilgrimage. The story may not be in history books, but it explains why it anchors so many travel memories.
history.originText: “Pub Street” (Khmer: ផ្លូវបារអាហារ / ផ្លូវហាងស្រា) literally means “bar street.” It is a short lane in Siem Reap’s old town known for dining and nightlife. The name comes from the many bars and restaurants clustered here; it is a local habit, not an official district name.
history.cultureText: The street sits next to the Old Market (Phsar Chas). By day it is an ordinary alley for locals; after dark it becomes a pedestrian leisure zone for travellers. Its rise is tied to Angkor tourism: as world visitors grew, family workshops gave way to bars, street BBQ and world music. Artists, musicians and volunteers also meet here, making it Siem Reap’s “living room” where ancient Angkor meets modern travellers.

night.title: Night Experience
night.subtitle: What makes an evening on Pub Street so memorable.

cards.title: Street Atmosphere
cards.text: When the lights come on, the street fills with people, music and the warm glow of restaurant signs. It is lively but relaxed — perfect for an evening stroll.

cards.title: Local Food
cards.text: From Khmer curries and BBQ to fried noodles, fruit shakes and sweets — the street is a casual open-air dining court for every budget.

cards.title: Entertainment
cards.text: Bars, live acoustic music and street performances line the lane. You can sit with a drink, listen to a band or simply watch the crowd go by.

daynight.title: Day vs Night
daynight.subtitle: Pub Street changes character through the day. Here is what to expect.

cards.label: Daytime
cards.text: Quiet and bright — good for photos, shopping and a relaxed walk before the crowds arrive.

cards.label: Evening
cards.text: Restaurants open and the first drinks appear. A relaxed, friendly vibe builds up.

cards.label: Night
cards.text: The busiest and most energetic time — music, lights and the fullest crowds.

daynight.note: Tip: go after 18:00 for the true Pub Street feeling, but earlier in the evening is calmer and more family-friendly.

map.title: How To Get There
map.subtitle: Pub Street is central and easy to reach from anywhere in Siem Reap.
map.hoursValue: Area open 24h; bars and restaurants from evening

modes.title: From Siem Reap–Angkor International Airport
modes.text: The airport is about 20–30 minutes by road from Pub Street. Taxis and tuk-tuks are available at the terminal.
steps: Exit the arrivals hall and head to the official taxi / tuk-tuk counter or ride-hailing pick-up area.
Agree the fare before boarding (a taxi is usually more than a tuk-tuk, which is the local open-air option).
Follow National Road 6 toward the city center, then turn toward the Old Market (Phsar Chas) area.
Ask the driver to drop you at 'Pub Street' or the Old Market — they are adjacent and well known.

modes.title: From Angkor Wat
modes.text: Pub Street sits about 7 km north of the temple area; a short tuk-tuk ride brings you back into town.
steps: After your temple visit, find a tuk-tuk near the Angkor ticket checkpoint or main entrance.
Show the driver 'Pub Street / Old Market' — most drivers know it by name.
The ride heads south into central Siem Reap and takes roughly 15–20 minutes depending on traffic.

modes.title: Around the city center
modes.text: Pub Street is compact and walkable from most central hotels and the riverside.
steps: From the Old Market (Phsar Chas), walk one block east — Pub Street is right beside it.
From the Siem Reap River promenade, head one block inland (west) toward the Old Market.
At night the street becomes a pedestrian zone, so simply follow the lights and music.

nearby.title: Nearby Attractions
nearby.subtitle: Worth exploring before or after your evening on Pub Street.

places.name: Old Market (Phsar Chas)
places.text: A traditional market for souvenirs, snacks and local life, right beside Pub Street.

places.name: Angkor Night Market
places.text: A nighttime shopping area with handicrafts, clothes and street food stalls.

places.name: Siem Reap Riverside
places.text: A calm promenade along the river — nice for a post-dinner walk.

places.name: Angkor Wat
places.text: The world-famous temple complex and Cambodia's top heritage site, a short trip north.

food.title: Food Around Pub Street
food.intro: Pub Street is a great place to sample Cambodian flavors in a relaxed, casual setting. These are some dishes you will commonly find — presented as cultural context, not restaurant recommendations.

items.name: Amok
items.text: A gentle Khmer curry steamed in banana leaf, often with fish and coconut.

items.name: Khmer BBQ
items.text: Grilled meats and vegetables, sometimes cooked at your table.

items.name: Fried noodles
items.text: Quick, cheap and filling — a backpacker staple across the street.

items.name: Fruit shakes
items.text: Fresh blended tropical fruit drinks, perfect in the warm evening.

items.name: Cambodian desserts
items.text: Sweet sticky-rice, custards and palm-sugar treats from small stalls.

reviews.title: Visitor Experience Summary
reviews.subtitle: A balanced look at what travelers commonly say — based on public review trends, not copied comments.

pros.text: Lively, friendly atmosphere that is easy to enjoy.
Central and walkable, close to the Old Market.
Great for an evening stroll and people-watching.

cons.text: Crowded at peak hours (evenings and weekends).
Quite commercial compared with the rest of the city.

practical.title: Practical Tips
practical.subtitle: Neutral advice for independent travellers to plan with more ease.

cards.title: Stay aware
cards.text: It is a popular tourist area. Keep normal travel caution with belongings.

cards.title: Getting around
cards.text: Walk or take a tuk-tuk. The area is central and compact.

cards.title: Money
cards.text: Cash is handy for small stalls; many bars and restaurants take cards.

cards.title: Timing
cards.text: Arrive after 18:00 for the full lights-and-music experience.

items.v: Liveliest from lighting-up to midnight; for a quiet stroll, go afternoon to before sunset.
A pedestrian leisure zone, best on foot; alleys connect, watch your belongings.
Most places take cash and major e-payments; small cash helps bargaining and tips.
Generally safe; guard belongings, drink responsibly, mind night traffic and steps.
English is widely used in the tourist area; a few Khmer greetings go a long way.
Good for families by day; at night it is crowded and loud—plan accordingly if with infants or needing quiet.

gallery.title: Pub Street Gallery
gallery.subtitle: A glimpse of the street, its food and its night-life energy.

items.a: The street area is accessible any time, but restaurants and nightlife operate mainly in the evening. The surrounding lanes are open around the clock.
It is generally a popular, well-visited tourist area. Visitors should keep normal travel awareness — watch belongings and use licensed tuk-tuks.

items.q: How long should I spend there?
items.a: Usually 1–3 hours is enough to eat, drink and explore the lane at a relaxed pace.

items.q: Is Pub Street suitable for families?
items.a: Yes — early evening is the most suitable time for families, before the crowds and late-night energy peak.

amenities.title: Nearby Facilities & Services
amenities.subtitle: Listed to help you plan your visit. We describe only the type and general availability of services, and do not endorse any specific business. Verify locations and opening hours on site before your visit.

items.v: Restrooms are available in restaurants, cafés and shopping venues along the street; some public areas have paid facilities.
items.note: Prefer facilities inside dining venues; open-air options are limited at night.

items.v: Several open-air lots and hotel valet parking exist nearby; spaces around the Old Market get tight in the evening.
items.note: At peak hours, park a bit further and walk, or use other transport.

items.v: Mostly bars, restaurants, BBQ stalls and street food, covering Khmer, Asian and international cuisines.
items.note: Choose by budget and cuisine; check public reviews rather than a specific name.

items.v: From hostels and boutique hotels to upscale resorts, concentrated around the Old Market and west riverbank.
items.note: Pick by budget and quietness; street-facing rooms can be lively at night.

items.v: Within walking distance: convenience stores, groceries and souvenir markets for daily needs, drinks and small items.
items.note: The night market near the Old Market is best for souvenirs.

items.v: Fuel stations are spread across the city; EV and phone charging are available at hotels, cafés and malls.
items.note: If renting a vehicle, top up before long trips.

items.v: ATMs and money changers near main streets and malls accept major cards.
items.note: Prefer ATMs inside bank branches; mind cross-border fees.

items.v: Pharmacies, clinics and international medical points are in the city; contact local ambulance and tourist police in emergencies.
items.note: Get travel insurance and save embassy contacts.

items.v: Most dining and lodging offer free Wi-Fi; tourist SIM cards are sold at local kiosks.
items.note: Be careful with public networks in crowded areas.
